PREFACE
This Code constitutes a recodification of the general and permanent ordinances of the City of Conyers, Georgia.
Source materials used in the preparation of the Code were the 1990 Code, as updated through May 4, 2011, and ordinances subsequently adopted by the Mayor and Council. The source of each section is included in the history note appearing in parentheses at the end thereof. The absence of such a note indicates that the section is new and was adopted for the first time with the adoption of the Code. By use of the comparative tables appearing in the back of this Code, the reader can locate any section of the 1990 Code, as updated, and any subsequent ordinance included herein.
Notes which tie related sections of the Code together and which refer to relevant state law have been included. A table listing the state law citations and setting forth their location within the Code is included at the back of this Code.
Title, Chapter and Section Numbering System
The title, chapter and section numbering system used in this Code is the same system used in many state and local government codes. Each section number consists of three parts separated by a dash. The first figure before the dash refers to the title number, the second figure after the first dash refers to the chapter number, and the figure after the last dash refers to the position of the section within the chapter. Thus, the second section of title 1, chapter 1 is numbered 1-1-2, and the first section of chapter 6 of title 2 is 2-6-1. Under this system, each section is identified with its title and chapter, and at the same time, new sections can be inserted in their proper place by using the decimal system for amendments. For example, if new material consisting of one section that would logically come between sections 2-6-1 and 2-6-2 is desired to be added, such new section would be numbered 2-6-1.5. New chapters and new articles may be included in the same way or, in the case of chapters, may be placed at the end of the title embracing the subject, and, in the case of articles, may be placed at the end of the chapter embracing the subject. The next successive number shall be assigned to the new chapter or article. New titles can be inserted in their proper place by using the decimal system.
Page Numbering System
The page numbering system used in this Code is a prefix system. The letters to the left of the colon are an abbreviation which represents a certain portion of the volume. The number to the right of the colon represents the number of the page in that portion. In the case of a chapter of the Code, the number to the left of the colon indicates the number of the chapter. In the case of an appendix to the Code, the letter immediately to the left of the colon indicates the letter of the appendix. The following are typical parts of codes of ordinances, which may or may not appear in this Code at this time, and their corresponding prefixes:

Indexes
The indexes have been prepared with the greatest of care. Each particular item has been placed under several headings, some of which are couched in lay phraseology, others in legal terminology, and still others in language generally used by local government officials and employees. There are numerous cross references within the indexes themselves which stand as guideposts to direct the user to the particular item in which the user is interested.
Looseleaf Supplements
A special feature of this publication is the looseleaf system of binding and supplemental servicing of the publication. With this system, the publication will be kept up to date. Subsequent amendatory legislation will be properly edited, and the affected page or pages will be reprinted. These new pages will be distributed to holders of copies of the publication, with instructions for the manner of inserting the new pages and deleting the obsolete pages.
Keeping this publication up to date at all times will depend largely upon the holder of the publication. As revised pages are received, it will then become the responsibility of the holder to have the amendments inserted according to the attached instructions. It is strongly recommended by the publisher that all such amendments be inserted immediately upon receipt to avoid misplacing them and, in addition, that all deleted pages be saved and filed for historical reference purposes.

ORDINANCE NO. 859
AN ORDINANCE ADOPTING AND ENACTING A NEW CODE FOR THE CITY OF CONYERS GEORGIA; PROVIDING FOR THE REPEAL OF CERTAIN ORDINANCES NOT INCLUDED THEREIN; PROVIDING A PENALTY FOR THE VIOLATION THEREOF; PROVIDING FOR THE MANNER OF AMENDING SUCH CODE; PROVIDING WHEN SUCH CODE AND THIS ORDINANCE SHALL BECOME EFFECTIVE; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.
NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED that it is the intention of the City Council and it hereby is ordained by the authority of same:
SECTION 1. The Code entitled "The Code of the City of Conyers, Georgia", which is published by Municipal Code Corporation, consisting of Titles 1 through 12, each inclusive, is hereby adopted.
SECTION 2. All ordinances of a general and permanent nature that were enacted on or before August 17, 2011 and that are not included in the Code or recognized and continued in force by reference therein, are hereby repealed.
SECTION 3. The repeal provided for in Section 2 hereof shall not be construed to revive any ordinance or part thereof that has been repealed by a subsequent ordinance that is repealed by this ordinance.
SECTION 4. In compliance with the Zoning Procedures Law, the following portions of the City of Conyers Code of Ordinances were publicly advertised and received review from the Conyers/Rockdale Planning Commission:
Title 8, Chapter 1: General Provisions
Title 8, Chapter 4: Floodplain Management and Flood Damage Prevention
Title 8, Chapter 5: Signs
Title 8, Chapter 7: Zoning
Title 8, Chapter 8: Mobile Homes
Title 8, Chapter 9: Historic Preservation
Title 8, Chapter 10: Tree Preservation and Landscape
Title 8, Chapter 11: Stormwater
Title 9, Chapter 10: Adult Entertainment Establishments
Said ordinances may or may not include amendments to zoning ordinances that change the text of said zoning ordinances. In addition, said ordinances may contain ordinances that do not pertain to zoning. Therefore, the City of Conyers has not made a legislative decision that all such sections constitute zoning ordinances.
SECTION 5. Unless another penalty is expressly provided, every person convicted of a violation of any provision of the Code or any ordinance, rule or regulation adopted or issued in pursuance thereof shall be punished by a fine not to exceed $1,000.00 and imprisonment in the County jail and work and labor on the streets or public works of the City, whether within or without the corporate limits, not exceeding six months, or both a fine and sentence of imprisonment and labor; and all sentences may be in the alternative and fines may be imposed with the alternative of sentence to imprisonment and labor if the fines are not paid. Each act of violation and each day upon which any such violation shall continue or occur shall constitute a separate offense. The penalty provided by this section, unless another penalty is expressly provided, shall apply to the amendment of any Code section, whether or not such penalty is reenacted in the amendatory ordinance. In addition to the penalty prescribed above, the City may pursue other remedies such as abatement of nuisances, injunctive relief and revocation of licenses or permits.
SECTION 6. Additions or amendments to the Code when passed in such form as to indicate the intention of the City to make the same a part of the Code shall be deemed to be incorporated in the Code, so that reference to the Code includes the additions and amendments.
SECTION 7. Ordinances adopted after August 17, 2011 that amend or refer to ordinances that have been codified in the Code shall be construed as if they amend or refer to like provisions of the Code.
SECTION 8. If any section, subsection, provisions, or clause of any part of this Ordinance shall be declared invalid or unconstitutional or, if the provisions of any part of this Ordinance as applied to any particular situation or set of circumstances shall be declared invalid or unconstitutional, such invalidity shall not be construed to affect the portions of this Ordinance not so held to be invalid, or the application of this Ordinance to other circumstances not so held to be invalid. It is hereby declared as the intent of the City Council that this Ordinance would have been adopted in its current form without the invalid or unconstitutional provision contained therein.
SECTION 9. Pursuant to Section 2-402(a)(4) of the Charter of the City of Conyers, Georgia, the second reading of this Ordinance is hereby waived in order to permit this Ordinance to become effective upon its adoption by the City Council and upon its execution by the Mayor.
ADOPTED AND APPROVED by the City Council of Conyers, Georgia this 18 th day of January, 2012.

In the construction of this Code and of all ordinances, the ordinary signification shall be applied to all words, except words of art, or words connected with a particular trade or subject-matter, when they shall have the signification attached to them by experts in such trade, or with reference to such subject matter; provided, the following definitions and rules of construction shall be observed, unless such definition or construction would be inconsistent with the manifest intent of the City Council:
(a) General rule. The City Council shall hold public hearings as required by all applicable ordinances and on such other matters as the City Council may, in its discretion, determine to hear through public hearings. The rules of procedure for such hearing shall be as follows:
(1) In order for a person in attendance at a public hearing to speak on a matter, such person shall register with the City Clerk or other person designated by the City prior to the time of the meeting at which such matter shall be heard by the Mayor and City Council. Such registration shall include:
(i) The name, address and telephone number of the person wishing to speak;
(ii) The matter on which the person wishes to speak;
(iii) Whether the person intends to speak as a proponent or opponent of the matter; and
(iv) Whether the person has been named as a representative to speak on behalf of a group.
(2) The Mayor shall review for those present these procedures and set forth the operating procedures for the hearing.
(3) The Mayor shall call the matter before the City Council.
(4) The matter shall be presented by the applicant or the Planning Commission Chairman or department or committee chairman, as the case may be, if deemed necessary by the Mayor.
(5) The Mayor shall then call the persons who have registered to speak on the matter. When a person is recognized to speak, he or she shall rise and begin by stating his or her name and address and the organization such person represents, if any.
(6) Each person who shall have registered in advance shall be allowed a total of two minutes to express opinions and make points on the proposed matter; provided however, that if a person has been named as a representative to speak on behalf of a group of proponents of a matter, such person shall be allotted a maximum total of ten minutes to express opinions and make points on the proposed matter, and if a person has been named as a representative to speak on behalf of a group of opponents of a matter, such person shall be allotted a maximum total of ten minutes to express opinions and make points on the proposed matter. For purposes of this section, a group shall consist of not less than five people.
(7) Proponents of the matter shall be allowed to speak first, and opponents of the matter shall be allowed to speak second; provided, however, that two minutes may be reserved by the proponents of a matter so that one person who has registered to speak as a proponent of a matter may speak on the matter in rebuttal after all opponents of a matter have spoken.
(8) No debate between speakers will be permitted.
(9) Debate or argument with the Mayor or City Council will not be permitted or tolerated.
(10) Speakers are expected to conduct themselves in an appropriate manner. The involvement of personalities or the use of abusive or profane language will not be tolerated. Speakers will be ruled out of order for such infractions.
(11) At the conclusion of the oral presentation by the proponents and opponents of the matter, the Mayor and City Council will be afforded an opportunity to ask questions of the planning commission chairman or department or committee chairman, as the case may be, or the proponents or opponents of the matter for the purpose of clarification or obtaining additional information.
(12) The applicant or the planning commission chairman or department or committee chairman, as the case may be, shall then make his or her recommendation to the Mayor and City Council and any discussion among the Mayor and City Council shall be conducted at this time.
(13) The Mayor and City Council shall then consider the several presentations, evaluate other pertinent data, and vote on the application. The vote may be for approval, denial, deferral, or postponement of a vote until a later date; provided, however, that in the event of a postponement of the vote, all interested parties shall be notified of the date, time, and place at which a vote on the matter will occur.
(14) The Mayor and City Council may dispense with any or all of these procedures by majority vote of the members of the City Council present at the meeting.

When used in this article, the following words and phrases have the meaning ascribed to them in this section, unless the context indicates a different meaning:
(1) Accrual basis means the basis of accounting under which revenues are recorded when earned or when levies are made, and expenditures are recorded as soon as they result in liabilities, notwithstanding that the receipt of the revenue or payment of the expenditure may take place, in whole or in part, in another accounting period.
(2) Appropriation means an authorization granted by the City Council to make expenditures or to incur obligations for specific purposes.
(3) Appropriation balance means unencumbered balance of appropriation or allotment, and unexpended balance of appropriation or allotment.
(4) Assets means property of all kinds of a government, including both current assets and fixed assets.
(5) Audit means the examination of records, documents, reports, systems of internal control, accounting and financial procedures, and other evidence for one or more of the following purposes:
a. To ascertain whether the statements prepared from the accounts present fairly the financial position and the results of financial operations of the constituent funds and balanced account groups of the governmental unit in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles applicable to governmental units and on a basis consistent with that of the preceding year;
b. To determine the propriety, legality, and mathematical accuracy of a governmental unit's financial transactions;
c. To ascertain whether all financial transactions have been properly recorded; and
d. To ascertain the stewardship of public officials who handle and are responsible for the financial resources of a governmental unit.
(6) Balance sheet means a statement ordinarily prepared from books kept by double entry showing assets, liabilities, reserves and surplus of a fund of a governmental unit at specified date properly classified to exhibit financial position of the fund or unit at that date.
(7) Budget means a plan of financial operation embodying an estimate of proposed expenditures for a given time and the proposed means of financing them. The annual budget refers to a period of one year.
(8) Budgetary control means the control of management of a government unit in accordance with an approved budget and keeping expenditures within the limitations of available appropriations or revenues.
(9) Cash basis means the system of accounting under which revenues are accounted for only when received in cash, and expenditures are accounted for only when paid.
(10) Contingent account means an appropriation to provide for unforeseen expenditures.
(11) Current surplus means the excess of the current assets of a fund over its current liabilities and reserves.
(12) Debit and credit. Terms commonly used to indicate the manner in which a transaction is to be recorded. Every entry on the left side of the ledger sheet is called a "debit." Every entry on the right side of the ledger sheet is called a "credit."
(13) Debt service means the amount of money necessary annually to pay the interest on the outstanding debt and the principal of maturing bonded debt not payable from a sinking fund and to provide a fund for the redemption of bonds payable from a sinking fund.
(14) Delinquent taxes means taxes remaining unpaid on and after the date on which a penalty for nonpayment is attached. Even though the penalty may be subsequently waived and a portion of the taxes may be abated or cancelled, the unpaid balances continue to be delinquent taxes until abated, cancelled, or converted into tax liens.
(15) Encumbrances means obligations in the form of purchase orders, contracts or salary commitments which are chargeable to an appropriation and for which a part of the appropriation is reserved.
(16) Fund means a sum of money or other resources (gross or net) set aside for the purpose of carrying on specific activities or to attain certain objectives in accordance with special regulations, restrictions, or limitations. A fund is a distinct financial and legal entity.
(17) Internal audit means an audit made by persons on the staff of the government unit whose accounts are being audited primarily for the purpose of internal control. An internal audit is usually a continuous audit.
(18) Liabilities means debts owed.
(19) Millage means a term used to express the property tax rate and derived from the term "mill," which is one-tenth of a cent. Thus, ten mills equal $0.01 or one percent. (Millage is determined by dividing the total amount of money to be raised by the total assessed value of the Municipality.)
(20) Taxes receivable means the uncollected portion of taxes which a government unit has levied.
(21) Trust funds means amounts received or appropriated and held in trust in accordance with an agreement or legislative act which may be expended only in accordance with the terms of such trust or act.
(Code 1978, § 3-1003; Code 1990, § 3-1-4)

(a) The City Manager or his/her designee may refund to a taxpayer any and all taxes and license fees which are determined to have been erroneously or illegally assessed and collected from such taxpayer under the laws of the State, under resolution or ordinance of the City or which are determined to have been voluntarily or involuntarily overpaid by the taxpayer.
(b) In any case in which it is determined that an erroneous or illegal collection of any tax or license fee has been made by the City or that a taxpayer has voluntarily or involuntarily overpaid any tax or license fee, the taxpayer from whom the tax or license fee was collected may file a claim for a refund with the City at any time within one year or (in the case of taxes) three years after the date of the payment of the tax or license fee to the City. The taxpayer shall make the claim for refund in writing on a form provided by the City; the form shall contain at a minimum the following information:
(1) The taxpayer's name;
(2) The taxpayer's address;
(3) A summary of the statement of the grounds upon which the taxpayer relies; and
(4) Whether the taxpayer desires a conference or hearing before the City in connection with any claim for a refund.
(c) If the claim is properly submitted, the City Manager or his/her designee shall consider the information contained in the taxpayer's claim for a refund and such other information as is available. The City Manager or his/her designee shall approve or disapprove the taxpayer's claim and shall notify the taxpayer of its action.
(1) In the event any claim for refund is approved, the City shall refund such amount within 60 days of the date of the approval of the taxpayer's claim; provided, however, the City Manager or his/her designee may apply such refund to any delinquent accounts owed to the City by the taxpayer. No refund provided for herein shall be assignable.
(2) Any taxpayer whose claim for a refund is denied by the City Council or whose claim is neither denied nor approved within one year from the date of the filing of the claim, shall have the right to bring an action for a refund in the Superior Court of the County.
(3) No action or proceeding for the recovery of a refund shall be commenced before the expiration of one year from the date of filing the claim for refund unless the City renders a decision on the claim within the one year period. No action or proceeding for the recovery of a refund shall be commenced after the expiration of one year from the date the claim is denied. The one-year period described in this subsection for filing an action for a refund shall be extended for such period as may be agreed upon in writing between the taxpayer and the City Council during the one-year period or any extension of the one-year period.
(4) Refunds as provided for herein and approved or allowed shall be paid from the funds of the City to which the tax or license fees were originally paid. Such refunds shall be paid within 60 days of the approval of the taxpayer's claim or within 60 days of the entry of a final decision in any action for a refund.
(d) The City Manager or his/her designee shall be responsible for the administration of this section and shall be authorized to make such other rules and regulations and establish such policies as are necessary to implement this chapter.

For the purposes of this article, the following terms shall have the following meanings respectively ascribed to them, unless the context indicates a different meaning.
(1) Reserved.
(2) Certificate of authority means a document issued by the City Manager or his/her designee following registration by a person with the City as an innkeeper, which shall authorize such innkeeper to collect the tax levied and assessed pursuant to this article.
(3) Collection allowance means the percentage of the gross taxes due that an innkeeper may retain as a compensation for expenses incurred in collecting, submitting, reporting and paying taxes pursuant to this article.
(4) Deficiency means the amount by which the tax remitted by an innkeeper is less than the amount that should have been paid for the same period, as determined by the City Manager or his/her designee, and encompasses both underpayment of tax and nonpayment of tax.
(5) Due date means the day of the month designated hereinafter as the day on or before which innkeepers must submit the statements and reports required under this article and remit to the City the taxes due for the immediately preceding month.
(6) Gross taxes means the total of taxes due pursuant to this article on the gross rental charges collected by an innkeeper in a given month, prior to deduction of the collection allowance provided for herein.
(7) Innkeeper means any person, including but not limited to the owner or proprietor of the premises, lessee, sub-lessee, lender in possession, licensee or any other person or entity, licensed by or required to pay business or occupation taxes to the City for operating a hotel, motel, inn, lodge, tourist camp, tourist cabin, campground, or any other place in which rooms, lodgings, or accommodations are regularly furnished for value. Said term encompasses every person legally subject to such licensure or business or occupation tax, whether or not such person actually complies with such license or business or occupation tax requirements.
(8) Lodging means any room, lodging, or accommodation occupied, intended to be occupied or furnished, or offered to the public for occupancy by one or more occupants, in a hotel, motel, inn, lodge, tourist camp, tourist cabin, campground, or any other place in which rooms, lodgings, or accommodations are regularly furnished or offered to the public for occupancy for value.
(9) Month or monthly period means the calendar months of any year.
(10) Net taxes means the total of taxes due pursuant to this article on the gross rental charges collected by an innkeeper in a given month, after deduction of the collection allowance provided for herein.

(13) Occupant means any person or entity that for consideration uses, possesses, or has the right to use or possess lodging as defined herein.

(17) Return means the monthly report or form as may be required by the City Manager or his/her designee to be completed by an innkeeper to convey to the City such information as may be necessary or expedient for the administration of this article.
(18) Tax or excise tax means the tax imposed by this article.

(1) Authority. The City Manager or his/her designee shall administer and enforce this article for the levy and collection of the tax under this article.

(4) Innkeeper registration; certificate of authority. Every person engaged in or about to engage in the operation of a hotel, motel, inn, lodge, tourist camp, tourist cabin, campground, or any other place in which rooms, lodgings, or accommodations are regularly furnished or offered to the public for occupancy for value in the City shall register with the City Manager or his/her designee as an innkeeper on a form provided by the City Manager. Persons engaged in said business must so register not later than 15 days after first becoming subject to this article, but the failure to register shall not relieve any person from the obligation of collection or remittance of the tax. The registration shall be signed by the owner if a natural person; in case of ownership by an association or partnership, by a member or a partner; in the case of ownership by a corporation, by an executive officer or some other person specifically authorized by the corporation to sign the registration. The City Manager or his/her designee shall after the registration issue, without charge, a certificate of authority to each innkeeper to collect the tax from occupants. A separate registration shall be required for each place of business of an innkeeper. Each certificate of authority shall state the name and location of the business to which it is issued and shall be prominently displayed therein so as to be seen and to come readily to the notice of all occupants and persons seeking occupancy. The certificates of authority shall be nonassignable and nontransferable and shall be returned immediately to the City Manager upon the cessation of business at the location named or upon sale or transfer of the business at that location.
(5) Election of cash or accrual basis. As part of the registration with the City Manager or his/her designee as an innkeeper, each innkeeper must make an election as to remittance of tax on a cash basis or accrual basis, as those terms are defined by generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). Once an election of cash basis or accrual basis is made, an innkeeper may not thereafter change its election without the prior written consent of the City Manager or his/her designee.
(a) Any innkeeper reporting on the cash basis of accounting shall include in each return all cash rental charges made during the period covered by the return and all collections made in any period on credit rental charges of prior periods and shall remit the tax on the rental charges at the time of filing the return.

(1) Due date. The tax shall become due and payable by the occupant at the time of occupancy. The due date for innkeepers to file returns and remit taxes to the City shall be the 20th day of each month.
(2) Return. On or before the 20th day of each month following the first month an innkeeper shall be liable for collection and remittance of the tax, such innkeeper shall transmit to the City Manager or his/her designee for the City, a return in such form as the City Manager or his/her designee may prescribe. The City Manager or his/her designee may require innkeepers to provide such additional information as he/she may deem necessary or expedient for the administration of this article.
(3) Remittance of tax. Along with said return, the innkeeper shall remit to the City Manager or his/her designee on or before the due date, the net taxes due for the immediately preceding month.
(4) Allocation of payments. Payments made shall be allocated first to any unpaid penalties, second to any unpaid tax and third to interest.
(5) Penalty for return filed after due date. Any return filed with the City Manager or his/her designee after the due date shall subject the innkeeper to a penalty of five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, if the failure is for one month or less; and an additional five percent or $5.00, whichever is greater, for each additional month or fraction thereof in which such failure shall continue; provided, however, that the aggregate penalty for any single violation shall not exceed 25 percent or $25.00, whichever is greater.
(6) Interest on taxes paid after due date. Any tax not remitted to the City Manager or his/her designee on or before the due date shall accrue interest on the unpaid principal amount due, computed at the rate of one percent per month.
(Code 1990, § 3-2-56; Ord. No. 706, 5-18-2005)
262:
(1) Service of notice to innkeeper. If the City Manager or his/her designee is not satisfied with a return or the amount of tax paid to the City by any innkeeper or if an innkeeper fails to make a return required hereunder, the City Manager or his/her designee shall notify the innkeeper that a determination of deficiency is being undertaken. The notice may be served personally or by United States mail; if by United States mail, the service shall be addressed to the innkeeper at the innkeeper's address as it appears in the records of the City Manager or his/her designee. For service by United States mail of any notice required by this article, the service is complete when delivered by certified mail with a receipt signed by the addressee, or when made by statutory overnight delivery.
(2) Time limit for service of notice of intent to determine deficiency. Except for cases involving fraud, intent to evade this article or authorized rules or regulations, or failure to make a return, every notice of intent to make a determination of deficiency shall be served within three years after the due date of the monthly period for which the tax is proposed to be recomputed to determine a deficiency, or within three years after the return is filed, whichever period should last expire. There shall be no limitation upon the time within which notice of intent to make a determination of deficiency must be served for cases involving fraud, intent to evade this article or authorized rules or regulations, or failure to make a return.
(3) Response by innkeeper. The innkeeper shall have the right to submit to the City Manager or his/her designee within 30 days of service of the notice of intent to make a determination of deficiency, such documentation in support of the accuracy of its return and the tax remitted therewith as the innkeeper may desire.
(4) Determination of tax.
(a) Underpayment of tax or irregularity in return. If the City Manager or his/her designee is not satisfied with the return or the amount of tax paid to the City by any innkeeper under this article, the City Manager or his/her designee shall recompute the tax due for each monthly period in question. In recomputing the tax, the City Manager or his/her designee shall make the best and most accurate estimate reasonably practicable based upon the information available to him/her at the time the estimate is made. Said recomputation may be based upon information provided by or obtained from the innkeeper, information contained in previous returns filed by the innkeeper, information regarding occupancy rates contained in the returns for the same period of similarly situated innkeepers, information regarding occupancy rates contained in the returns for the same period of all other innkeepers in the City, taking into account such factors as location, size and other factors as the City Manager or his/her designee may deem appropriate, or some combination of information to arrive at the best and most accurate estimate of tax reasonably practicable. The method and manner of the recomputation shall be within the sole discretion of the City Manager or his/her designee. One or more deficiency determinations may be made of the tax due for one or more monthly periods.
(b) Failure to make return. If any innkeeper fails to make a return for the tax levied in this article for 30 or more days after the due date of said return, the City Manager or his/her designee shall make an estimate of the amount of the gross receipts of the innkeeper. The estimate shall be made for the period in respect to which the innkeeper failed to make the return. The City Manager or his/her designee shall make the best and most accurate estimate reasonably practicable based upon the information available to him/her at the time the estimate is made. Said estimate may be based upon information provided by or obtained from the innkeeper, information contained in previous returns filed by the innkeeper, information regarding occupancy rates contained in the returns for the same period of similarly situated innkeepers, information regarding occupancy rates contained in the returns for the same period of all other innkeepers in the City, taking into account such factors as location, size and other factors as the City Manager or his/her designee may deem appropriate, or some combination of information to arrive at the best and most accurate estimate of tax reasonably practicable. The method and manner of the estimate shall be within the sole discretion of the City Manager or his/her designee. Upon the basis of this estimate, the City Manager or his/her designee shall compute and determine the amount of tax required to be paid the City, adding to the sum thus determined a penalty as provided in Section 3-2-56(5). One or more determinations may be made for one or more periods.
(5) Interest on deficiency. The unpaid balance of the deficiency, exclusive of penalties, shall bear interest at the rate of one percent per month or any fraction of a month from the due date for the period in question until the date of payment.
(6) Offsetting of overpayments. Whenever the City Manager or his/her designee has made a determination of a deficiency for one or more monthly periods, the City may use overpayments from another or other period(s) to offset such deficiency and any penalties or interest due thereon.
(7) Penalty for negligence or disregard for rules and regulations. Should the City Manager or his/her designee determine that any part of the deficiency for which a deficiency determination has been made is due to negligence or disregard of the provisions of this article or the rules and regulations authorized hereunder, a penalty as provided in Section 3-2-56(5) shall be added thereto.
(8) Penalty for fraud or intent to evade. Should the City Manager or his/her designee determine that any part of the deficiency for which a deficiency determination is made is due to fraud or an intent to evade any section of this article or the rules and regulations authorized hereunder, a penalty of 50 percent of the deficiency will be added thereto.
(9) Notice of deficiency, interest and penalty. Should the City Manager or his/her designee make a determination that a deficiency exists, the City Manager or his/her designee shall forthwith notify the innkeeper of the monthly period(s) for which a deficiency was determined, the amount of such deficiency(ies), the date such determination was made, any penalty(ies) or interest applicable to such deficiency(ies) and the date by which the deficiency(ies) and penalty(ies) must be paid. Notice shall be given in the same manner as provided in Subsection (1) of this section for notice of intention to make a determination of deficiency.
(10) Innkeeper selling or quitting business.
(a) Final return. If any innkeeper liable for any amount under this article sells out his/her business or quits his/her business, he/she shall make a final return and remittance within 15 days after the date of selling or quitting the business.
(b) Withholding delinquent tax on sale of business. If any innkeeper liable for any amount under this article transfers or sells its business or quits the business, its successors or assigns shall withhold sufficient amounts from the purchase price to cover the amount required to be paid pursuant to this article until the former owner or operator of the innkeeper produces a receipt from the City Manager or his/her designee showing that the tax and any penalties and interest thereon has been paid or a certificate stating that no amount is due. If the purchaser of a business or innkeeper fails to withhold from the purchase price as required herein such purchaser shall be personally liable for the payment of the amount of the outstanding tax required to be withheld by him to the extent of such purchase price.
(11) Collection of deficiency.
(a) Security. Whenever an innkeeper shall have failed to substantially comply with the provisions of this article and the City Manager or his/her designee deems it necessary to ensure compliance with this article, the City Manager or his/her designee may require any innkeeper to deposit with the City Manager or his/her designee such security as the City Manager or his/her designee may prescribe. The amount of the security shall be fixed by the City Manager or his/her designee but shall not be greater than twice the innkeeper's estimated average liability for the period for which the innkeeper files returns, determined in such a manner as the City Manager or his/her designee deems proper, or $10,000.00, whichever amount is the lesser. The amount of the security may be increased by the City Manager or his/her designee subject to the limitations provided in this subsection. The City Manager or his/her designee may sell the security at public auction, with the approval of the Mayor and Council, if it becomes necessary to do so in order to recover any tax or any amount required to be collected, interest or penalty due. Notice of the sale may be served upon the innkeeper who deposited the security personally or by mail; if by mail, service shall be given in the same manner as provided in Subsection (1) of this section for notice of intention to make a determination of deficiency and shall be addressed to the innkeeper at the innkeeper's address as it appears in the records of the City Manager or his/her designee. Upon any sale, any surplus above the amounts due shall be returned to the innkeeper who deposited the security.
(b) Action for collection. At any time within three years after any tax becomes due and payable and at any time within three years after City Manager or his/her designee shall have determined a deficiency exists, the City Manager or his/her designee may bring an action in the courts of this state, of any other state, or of the United States in the name of the City to collect the amount delinquent, together with penalties and interest, court fees, filing fees, attorney's fees and other legal fees incident thereto.
(12) Refunds or credits for overpayment. Whenever any tax or interest has been paid more than once, overpaid, or has been erroneously or illegally collected or received by the City under this article, it may be refunded by the City. If a person or innkeeper determines that he has overpaid or paid more than once, which fact has not been determined by the City, he shall have three years from the date of payment to file a claim with the City Manager, in writing, stating the specific ground upon which the claim is founded. The claim shall be audited. If the claim is approved by the City, the excess amount paid may be credited on any amounts then due and payable from the person or innkeeper by whom it was paid or his administrators, executors or successors in interest as he may direct, or shall be refunded if no amount then remains due and payable.
(Code 1990, § 3-2-57; Ord. No. 706, 5-18-2005)

(19) Yard trimmings means plant material (leaves, grass clippings, branches, brush, flowers, roots, wood waste, etc.); debris commonly thrown away in the course of maintaining yards and gardens, including sod; and biodegradable or compostable waste approved for the yard trimmings programs. It shall be the duty of the owner of any premises to keep all refuse pending collection and disposal as follows:
(1) All garbage shall be free from liquid and placed in watertight paper or plastic bags and the tops secured and placed in an approved refuse receptacle. Receptacles adequate to hold the refuse normally accumulating between scheduled removals shall be provided on each premises.
(2) Other household refuse and other nonputrescible waste will be containerized in approved refuse receptacles or in disposable containers such as a box, watertight paper bag or plastic bag. No such refuse, refuse containers, or rubbish shall be placed or piled on the curb in a location or manner as to impede passengers of commercial passenger vehicles from boarding or departing from vehicles at places designated for vehicles to stop or let passengers on or off.
(3) Tree branches and heavy brush shall be cut in lengths not exceeding four feet in length completely trimmed, stacked in a compact pile on the curb, or property line in the case of streets where curbing has not been installed, in front of the residence, but such piles shall not extend into the street or be laid upon the sidewalk. Sticks, hedge clippings and small brush shall be gathered together into bundles and tied securely so that each bundle does not exceed four feet in length nor weigh more than 50 pounds. No such container, tree branches or heavy brush shall be placed or piled on the curb in a location or manner as to impede passengers of commercial passenger vehicles from boarding or departing from vehicles at places designated for vehicles to stop or let passengers on or off. The City will not collect logs and limbs over four feet long and will not collect stumps that weigh 50 pounds or more.
(4) Leaves, limbs, grass or other trimmings shall be placed in an orderly manner so as not to obstruct the free and normal flow of any drainage system or the safe vision or movement of any system or the safe vision or movement of any pedestrian or vehicular traffic. Such debris shall not be placed in the gutter of any roadway at any time. Shrubbery clippings, vines, briars and other running plants must be separated from all other leaf and limbs placed near the street for collection. Dirt, rocks, grass roots and other plant roots containing soil shall not be collected.
(5) Items placed on vacant lots. Leaves or limbs put on vacant lots by owners or violators shall not be collected by the City Public Works and Transportation Department crews.
(6) Placement of items by persons other than the owners of the property. Limbs cut and placed near the street for collection by any person other than the owner of the property shall not be collected or hauled by the City Public Works and Transportation Department. Individuals or companies under contract to collect leaves, limbs or removal of trees shall haul and dispose of all such refuse. This requirement also applies to utility or railroad companies which trim vegetation away from wires, equipment or tracks to maintain their right-of-way. Should an owner desire more than one cart, the owner may apply for additional carts by completing a request form at the Department of Customer Service. The owner must pay a minimum deposit of the present cost of a cart, plus an additional yearly sanitation fee.
(7) Noncombustible trash, except as provided under Subsection (10) of this section, and liquids will not be collected by the City and shall be disposed of by other means.
(8) All refuse receptacles shall be kept clean and free of accumulated waste and shall be treated with an effective insecticide if necessary to prevent nuisance by owner or owners of property.
(9) Each owner shall prevent, or otherwise be held responsible for, unsightly accumulations of refuse upon the property occupied by the owner or public thoroughfares adjoining his or her property.
(10) Pet litter, disposable diapers and similar waste must be contained in a securely tied plastic bag and placed in a trash container at the curb.
(11) It shall be a violation of this chapter to place, or cause to be placed, any hazardous waste, including, without limitation, any acid, explosive material, inflammable liquids, or dangerous or corrosive material of any kind in any refuse can or container for collection.
(12) Inoperative or worn out privately used household appliances such as refrigerators, stoves, washing machines, dryers, or discarded furniture will be collected at the curb on an on-call basis to the Public Works and Transportation Department.

After the verification process has been completed, the Department of Public Works and Transportation will conduct an engineering analysis to determine if the street(s) are eligible for speed breakers and if they would function properly. After such analysis, the Department of Public Works and Transportation shall make a recommendation to the Council as to whether a speed breaker district should be established.
(3) Petitions shall be coordinated by the owners or residents within the proposed speed breaker district. The City will not solicit signatures or gather support on behalf of the proposed district. The petition must designate a primary point of contact for communication purposes with the City.
(Code 1990, § 5-5-1; Ord. No. 1310, § 1, 1-18-2023)
340:
A "speed breaker district" is defined as a street, or portion of a street, or a system of streets within the City where speed breakers have been requested and/or installed.
(Code 1990, § 5-5-2; Ord. No. 1310, § 1, 1-18-2023)
341:
(1) Speed breakers will only be considered on streets categorized as residential.
(2) Speed breakers should only be used with no more than two traveled lanes.
(3) Speed breakers should not be placed within severe horizontal or vertical curves. The geometrics of the street must satisfy current residential guidelines, as defined by AASHTO (American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials) and/or City code.
(4) Street grade must be less than eight percent.
(5) Speed breakers should generally be installed where minimum safe stopping distance is available.
(6) Speed studies will be performed to confirm the existence of a speeding problem, which is as defined as the 85th percentile speed on the subject street(s) is 11 miles per hour or more over the posted speed limit, and also to ensure that speed breaker installation will address the speeding problem.
(7) Average daily traffic volume should be between 200 to 1,000 vehicles. Placement of breakers outside this range will require special evaluation.
(8) Speed breakers should not be installed on a street that carries a significant number (greater than five percent) of long wheelbase vehicles unless a reasonable alternative route exists for these vehicles.
(9) Speed breakers should not be installed on streets that are used as primary emergency vehicle access unless a reasonable alternative route exists for these vehicles.
(10) The type of speed breaker to be installed will be a flat-topped speed breaker.
(11) The maximum posted speed limit on any street requesting speed breakers will be 25 miles per hour.
(12) Adequate signing and marking at each speed breaker location shall be required.
(13) If the district is approved by Council, speed breakers shall be funded and installed by the City.
(14) If the speed-volume study reveals that the prevailing 85th percentile speed on the subject street(s) is not 11 mph or more over the posted speed limit of 25 miles per hour or if the average daily traffic is less than 200 vehicles or more than 1,000 vehicles, then at least 90 percent of the property owners or lessees (renters) within such proposed speed breaker district must approve of said installation.
(Code 1990, § 5-5-3; Ord. No. 1310, § 1, 1-18-2023)
342:
(1) The City will reassess the need for an existing speed breaker district upon presentation of a petition to the City, Department of Public Works and Transportation by 75 percent or more of the property owners or lessees (renters) within such speed breaker district, to determine if any reason exists to remove the speed breakers from the speed breaker district. The petition requesting a reassessment of a speed breaker district shall contain at a minimum the names (property owner and/or lessee, as applicable), property addresses and phone numbers of each person signing such petition. The petition shall be in such form as prescribed by the City. For a lessee to be eligible to sign the petition, the lessee must be engaged in a lease with the property owner within the proposed district for at least six months prior to signing the petition. A copy of each lease agreement must be submitted with the petition as proof of lease length and lessee's eligibility to sign. Only those persons listed on the lease agreement may sign the petition.
(2) Once a petition to reassess the speed breaker district has been filed with the City, then the Department of Public Works and Transportation will conduct a verification process to determine whether the petition complies with the requirements of this code section prior to any reassessment of the speed breaker district. After the verification process has been completed, the Department of Public Works and Transportation will conduct an engineering analysis to determine the traffic characteristics along the route and impact to the remaining street system. After an adequate review period of the engineering analysis, the City's Department of Public Works and Transportation will make a recommendation to the City Council as to whether to remove the speed breaker from the speed breaker district.
(3) Speed breakers must have been installed for a minimum of 12 months prior to submitting a petition to remove said speed breakers.
(4) If petition to reassess a speed breaker district or a petition to establish a speed breaker district does not meet requirements of the policy, or if the City Council denies approval of the petition, then the property owners and/or lessees must wait 12-months after the date of the denial prior to submitting another petition for the same speed breaker district.
(Code 1990, § 5-5-4; Ord. No. 1310, § 1, 1-18-2023)
343:
No speed breaker district shall be established or removed without the approval of the Council.
(Code 1990, § 5-5-5; Ord. No. 1310, § 1, 1-18-2023)
345:
(1) Upon written request for the installation of a sidewalk made by a property owner located on an existing City street and filed with the City, the City Manager or his/her designee shall conduct an evaluation to determine the appropriateness of the requested sidewalk installation.
